exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying an Expression by Expanding Parentheses and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we expand the parentheses:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \cos^2 x\left(\dfrac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}+\dfrac{1}{\cos x}+1\right) &=\cos^2 x\cdot \dfrac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}+\cos^2 x\cdot\dfrac{1}{\cos x}+\cos^2 x\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\cos^2 x\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}+\dfrac{\cos^2 x}{\cos x}+\cos^2 x\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\cancel{\cos^2 x}\sin^2 x}{\cancel{\cos^2 x}}+\dfrac{\cancel{\cos x} \cos x}{\cancel{\cos x}}+\cos^2 x\\[5pt] &=\sin^2 x+\cos x+\cos^2 x\\[5pt] &=\left(\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x\right)+\cos x\\[5pt] &=1+\cos x \end{align*}

Notice that, in the last step, we simplified the right-hand side using $\cos^2x +\sin^2 x = 1.$

Therefore, we conclude that

\[ \cos^2 x\left(\dfrac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}+\dfrac{1}{\cos x}+1\right)= 1+\cos x . \]

example.title: Simplifying an Expression by Expanding Parentheses and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we expand the parentheses:

\begin{align} \require{cancel} (\sin x - \cos x)^2 + (\sin x + \cos x)^2 &=(\sin^2x + \cos^2x - 2\sin x \cos x) + (\sin^2x + \cos^2x + 2\sin x \cos x) \\[3pt] &=(\sin^2x + \cos^2x - \cancel{2\sin x \cos x}) + (\sin^2x + \cos^2x + \cancel{2\sin x \cos x}) \\[3pt] &=\sin^2x + \cos^2x+ \sin^2x + \cos^2x\\[3pt] &=2\sin^2x + 2\cos^2x \\[3pt] &= 2(\sin^2x + \cos^2x) \end{align}

Then, we use $\sin^2{x} + \cos^2{x} = 1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses. This gives:

\begin{align} 2(\sin^2x + \cos^2x) = 2\cdot (1) = 2 \end{align}

Therefore, we conclude that

\[ (\sin x - \cos x)^2 + (\sin x + \cos x)^2 = 2 . \]

exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.text: Simplify the trigonometric expression $\sin^2 x\cos^3x +\sin^4 x\cos x.$
question.explanation:
First, we factor the expression:

\[ \sin^2 x\cos^3x +\sin^4 x\cos x = \sin^2 x\cos x\cdot \left(\cos^2 x+\sin^2 x\right) \]

Then, we use $\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

\begin{align*} \sin^2 x\cos x\cdot \left(\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x\right) & = \sin^2 x\cos x\cdot 1 \\ &= \sin^2 x\cos x \end{align*}

We conclude that

\[ \sin^2 x\cos^3x +\sin^4 x\cos x = \sin^2 x\cos x . \]

example.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we factor the expression:

\[ \sin{x} + 2\cos^3{x} + 2\sin^2{x}\cos{x} = \sin{x} + 2\cos{x}(\cos^2{x} + \sin^2{x}) \]

Then, we use $\cos^2{x} + \sin^2{x} = 1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

\begin{align*} \sin{x} + 2\cos{x}(\cos^2{x} + \sin^2{x}) &= \sin{x} +2 \cos{x} \cdot 1\\[3pt] &= \sin{x} + 2\cos{x} \end{align*}

Hence, we conclude that \[ \sin{x} + 2\cos^3{x} +2 \sin^2{x}\cos{x} = \sin{x} + 2\cos{x} . \]

exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying a Rational Expression Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we factor the denominator:

\[ \dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{\sin^5\theta+\sin^3\theta\cos^2\theta} = \dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{\sin^3\theta \cdot \left(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta\right)} \]

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible.

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{\sin^3\theta \cdot \left(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta\right)} & =\dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{\sin^3\theta\cdot 1}\\[5pt] & =\dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{\sin^3\theta }\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{\sin^2{\theta}\cdot \sin{\theta}} \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{\cancel{\sin^2\theta}\cos\theta}{\cancel{\sin^2{\theta}}\cdot \sin{\theta}}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\cos{\theta}}{\sin\theta} \\[5pt] &= \cot{\theta} \end{align*}

Hence, we conclude that

$$ \dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{\sin^5\theta+\sin^3\theta\cos^2\theta} = \cot\theta . $$

example.title: Simplifying a Rational Expression Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we factor $2\cos^2 x$ from the first two terms:

\[ \dfrac {2\cos^4{x} + 2\cos^2{x}\sin^2{x}-1}{\sin^2{x}} = \dfrac{2\cos^2{x}(\cos^2{x} + \sin^2{x})-1}{\sin^2{x}} \]

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible: \begin{align*} \dfrac{2\cos^2{x}(\cos^2{x} + \sin^2{x})-1}{\sin^2{x}} & = \dfrac{2\cos^2{x} -1}{\sin^2{x}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2\cos^2{x} -\left(\cos^2{x} + \sin^2{x}\right)}{\sin^2{x}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2\cos^2{x} - \cos^2{x} - \sin^2{x}}{\sin^2{x}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\cos^2{x} - \sin^2{x}}{\sin^2{x}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\cos^2{x}}{\sin^2{x}} - \dfrac{\sin^2{x}}{\sin^2{x}}\\[5pt] & = \cot^2{x} - 1 \end{align*}

Hence, we conclude that: \[ \dfrac{2\cos^4{x} + 2\cos^2{x}\sin^2{x}-1}{\sin^2{x}} = \cot^2{x} - 1 \]

exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying a Trigonometric Expression Using a Common Denominator and the Pythagorean Identity

question.text: Simplify the trigonometric expression $\sin x - \dfrac{\cos^2 x }{1-\sin x}.$
question.explanation:
We put both terms over a common denominator, and combine the two fractions:

\begin{align*} \sin x - \dfrac{\cos^2 x }{1-\sin x} &=\dfrac{\sin x}{1} - \dfrac{\cos^2 x }{1-\sin x} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{\sin x (1-\sin{x})}{1-\sin{x}} - \dfrac{\cos^2 x }{1-\sin x} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{\sin{x}(1-\sin{x}) - \cos^2{x}}{1-\sin x} \end{align*}

Finally, we simplify using the Pythagorean identity, as follows:

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\sin{x}(1-\sin{x}) - \cos^2{x}}{1-\sin x} & =\dfrac{\sin{x} - \sin^2{x} - \cos^2{x}}{1-\sin x} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\sin{x} - (\sin^2{x} + \cos^2{x})}{1-\sin x} \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{\sin{x} - 1}{1-\sin x} \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{-(1-\sin x)}{1-\sin x} \\[5pt] & =-1 \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that

\[ \sin x - \dfrac{\cos^2 x }{1-\sin x}=-1 . \]

example.title: Simplifying a Trigonometric Expression Using a Common Denominator and the Pythagorean Identity

question.text: Simplify the trigonometric expression $\dfrac{\cos^2 x }{1+\sin x}+\sin x.$
question.explanation:
We put both terms over a common denominator, and combine the two fractions:

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\cos^2 x }{1+\sin x}+\sin x &=\dfrac{\cos^2 x }{1+\sin x}+\dfrac{\sin x}{1} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{\cos^2 x }{1+\sin x}+\dfrac{\sin x(1+\sin x)}{1(1+\sin x)} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{\cos^2 x+\sin x(1+\sin x)}{1+\sin x} \end{align*}

Finally, we simplify using the Pythagorean identity, as follows:

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\cos^2 x+\sin x(1+\sin x)}{1+\sin x} & =\dfrac{\cos^2{x}+\sin x+\sin^2 x}{1+\sin{x}} \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{\left(\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x\right)+\sin x}{1+\sin{x}} \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{1+\sin{x}}{1+\sin{x}} \\[5pt] &= 1 \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that

\[ \dfrac{\cos^2 x }{2+\sin x}+\sin x=1 . \]
